title: Re3: A Holistic Framework and Dataset for Modeling Collaborative Document Revision
key_contributions: Re3: a holistic framework for joint analysis of collaborative document revision (review + revision + author response)
Re3-Sci: a large corpus of aligned scientific paper revisions manually labeled by action AND intent, supplemented with the peer reviews and human-written edit summaries
Provides first empirical insights into collaborative document revision in the academic domain
Assesses state-of-the-art LLMs at automating edit analysis and facilitating text-based collaboration
Releases annotation environment, protocols, data and experimental code
key_insight: A revision's correctness depends on the author's intent and the review that prompted it—not on surface similarity alone. The surrounding collaboration context (review comment, author response, edit summary) is what makes a revision interpretable.
direct_implication_for_skill: Version changes are often collaborative: a rule revision typically responds to a stakeholder request, a review comment, or a stated gap. The skill's 'interpretation', 'worked_example' and 'resolution_requirement' fields attempt to capture that intent, and this paper validates that design. It also suggests adding an optional 'rationale' input (why the change was made) alongside the old/new text, which would sharpen intent-based classification.
resolution_requirement_for_downstream: Different change types imply different downstream obligations: a semantic_shift forces evidence revalidation, a field_rename does not. Encoding intent lets the skill target revalidation only where it is required, instead of treating all 19 PRISMA deltas alike.
reading_notes: Read the abstract and Figure 1 (the review → revision → response loop). Useful as the framing paper for why 'why did this change' is a first-class question, not a footnote on 'what changed'.
